purpose: Define cleanup of rendezvous/signaling state after peer connection establishment, expiry or failure so bootstrap metadata does not become persistent application state.

topics.name: Rendezvous Bootstrap Cleanup
topics.purpose: Define cleanup of rendezvous/signaling state after peer connection establishment, expiry or failure so bootstrap metadata does not become persistent application state.

semantics.cleanup_rule: Signaling transaction and transient candidate state expire explicitly.
semantics.connected_rule: After P2P connection establishment, obsolete rendezvous state may be removed according to profile.
semantics.history_rule: Minimal audit/provenance evidence may remain without preserving unnecessary transient payload.
semantics.application_rule: Cleanup never deletes peer identity, IAM identity or application messages.
semantics.privacy_rule: Transient address metadata retention is bounded.

invariants.rule: Listener, route, endpoint, connection, channel, peer reachability and cryptographic transport evidence never by themselves grant application, data or operation authority.
Inbound network data remains inert until explicit protocol parsing, validation, identity/context resolution, authorization and dispatcher routing succeed.

hard_gates.condition: connection success leaves stale offers active indefinitely
cleanup inferred from file age only
